defects: Gate, real floater: right half of the porch roof (audit group at 1.88, 2.53, 3.7; 4 parts, 3.76 m wide), views 3-4: daylight slots show between the corrugated sheet and the log beam, and the sheet tip runs about 30 cm past the last post with nothing under it. A structural roof, not a hanging part.

Audit false positives: the 11 listed 0.49 m firewood groups (x about 3.7, y 0.34-1.0) are logs resting on the row below in the view 1 pile; no visible float. 7 further groups are not listed by the audit.
Chimney, views 2-3: courses are oversized blocks jutting 10-20 cm at random, like loose cubes stacked with no mortar, and nothing ties the stack to the wall.
Wall corner under the porch eave, views 3-4: a stray black timber stub pokes out of the corner and carries nothing.
Window, view 6: glass is a flat opaque plate with white mottling; logs stop dead at the jamb with no scribe or notch, and splinters stick up above the head.
Roof, view 5: an orange rust line of constant width follows every sheet lap in a regular grid; rust should run from nails and pool at the eaves.
Gable boards, view 6 top: a sky-coloured slit shows through the boarding.
Porch steps, views 3-4: two flat pads set off the deck edge, with no stringers or connection to the rim.
Gate not verified: tests/traversal.test.mjs does not exist, so the porch steps have no walk-through result.
fixes: Run rafters from the porch beam into the sheet with visible lag bolts and a ledger on the wall; trim the sheet to a 10 cm overhang past the last rafter.
Rebuild the chimney as course-true fieldstone with recessed mortar, stones 3-4 cm proud at most, a stepped footing and lead flashing at the eave.
Replace the window plate with a four-pane sash with glazing bars and one cracked pane; scribe the log ends to the frame and fit a sloped sill.
Repaint roof rust as streaks below nail lines and heavier eave bands; delete the lap grid.
Give the steps two notched stringers bolted to the rim joist; delete the stray stub at the wall corner and close the gable slit.

defects: Gate, real floater: rear fascia strip (audit group at 0, 3, -2; 4.9 m long), view 6: a sky-coloured slit runs the whole length between the strip and the roof slab.
Rear and side walls, view 6: block coursing is rotated and stretched into tall narrow slabs, while the door wall (view 4) has normal coursing.
All walls, views 1 and 6: cloudy mottling at even density reads as camouflage; no run-off below the roof edge and no ground splash at the base.
Door, view 4: flat green blotched slab held about 120 degrees open with no hinges, no frame rebate and no handle.
Fuse-box lid, views 1, 3, 4: a flat rust panel stands at right angles to the wall with no hinge, and in view 1 it pokes out past the corner.
Cable, views 2-3: an 8 m line leaves the rear corner with no conduit or wall entry and stops dead on the ground.
Body, views 1-2: a plain extruded box; the rear and two sides carry no detail at all.
fixes: Merge the rear fascia into the roof slab, or set it on the slab with a real drip edge so no daylight passes.
Reproject all walls to one coursing, 40 x 20 cm block with a running bond; add a corner return so courses wrap.
Replace the mottling with vertical stains under the roof edge, dark splash up to 30 cm at the base and rust bleed below the conduit.
Model door hinges, a steel frame and a lever handle; hinge the fuse-box lid on the box edge and keep it inside the wall line.
Route the cable through a conduit and wall gland, and end it at a junction post or a cut end.
Add a rear vent grille, a side downpipe and a concrete plinth with a broken corner.

defects: Gate, real floater: cooling fins and head (audit fins at y 0.86-1.05, head group at y 1.0+), crop of view 2: each fin is a separate plate with air gaps and no cylinder core; the head plate sits on them with nothing bolting through.
Gate, real floater: radiator (audit group at -0.92, 0.72, -0.06 and its separate slats), views 2-3: the panel stands 10-15 cm clear of the block, joined only by a thin hose.
Gate, real floater: exhaust (audit group at 0.41, 1.41, -0.37), views 1 and 6: the stack is twisted into a pinched bow-tie ribbon with inverted faces and does not seat on the manifold.
Control box, views 3-4: two round gauges above a small rectangular plate on four stilts read as a robot face; comic in a horror game.
Flywheel and crank, views 2-3: a shapeless black lump with a wire-thin handle that engages nothing.
Muffler, views 1-2 and 6: eight-sided sausage with black and orange blotches.
Air cleaner, views 1-4: a canister hanging off one thin bent tube with no bracket.
Skid, views 1-4: rust spots spaced evenly across flat faces; away from the edges, nothing explains them.
fixes: Rebuild the cylinder as one cast block with fins as real ribs on a core; bolt the head with four studs and nuts.
Mount the radiator on the skid with two angle-iron stays, a shroud to the block and two proper hoses with clamps.
Remodel the exhaust as a bent pipe with a flanged manifold joint, a straight stack and a rain flap.
Change the control box to a single gauge with switches, a cable gland and a stencil plate; break the two-eyes-and-mouth layout.
Model a spoked flywheel on a shaft with a keyway and a crank handle that seats on the shaft.
Restrict rust to weld lines, bolt heads and the skid's lower edges.

defects: Audit floaters ruled deliberate mounts: the whip group at y 34+ meets the tower head in the view 3 crop, and the dish at y 23.5 sits on a stub bracket against the leg in view 6. Neither is visibly detached. No cap.
All three dishes, views 3 and 6: the cream and dark mottling reads as a boulder, not a painted drum dish; no radome skin or feed horn.
Ladder, views 3 and 6: runs as a separate column beside a leg with no visible stand-off brackets.
Platform, view 6: black and white bars read as a stripe texture, not grating; there is no hatch where the ladder arrives.
Guy anchors, views 1-2: plain tilted concrete cubes; no turnbuckles or anchor eyes where the wires land.
Red and white banding, views 4-5: fades evenly with no peeling at joints or rust streaks below bolts.
Gate not verified: tests/traversal.test.mjs does not exist, so the ladder has no walk-through result.
fixes: Replace the dish texture with weathered off-white radome fabric, a dark rim band and a feed arm; add pipe clamps to the leg.
Add ladder stand-off brackets every 1.5 m and a cage from 3 m up.
Model the platform as an open grating with a hatch at the ladder head.
Add turnbuckles, thimbles and an anchor eye at each guy foot; bury 20 cm of each block.
Run rust streaks down from every bolted joint and flake the red paint at leg splices.

defects: Gate, real floater: landing top rails (audit groups at y 3.4, 10.6, 13.0, z +/-2.34; 1.96 m long), crop of view 2: bars cross the tower with free ends and no post under most of the span.
Audit false positives: catwalk, cab walls and roof (groups at y 14.9, 16.0, 18.0) read as carried on the legs and corner posts in views 1-5; no daylight visible. But no brackets are visible either.
Tower joints, crop of view 2: diagonals overlap and pass through each other and the legs with no gussets, bolts or plates.
Deck underside, views 1-4 top: unexplained daylight holes around the stair opening.
Roof, view 5: mottled black and orange patches read as camouflage.
Leg and brace material, view 6: ambiguous between weathered wood and painted steel; grain runs the same on every member.
Review framing: the cab is cropped in views 1-4 and 6, so only view 5 shows it.
Gate not verified: tests/traversal.test.mjs does not exist, so the stairs have no walk-through result.
fixes: Extend landing rail posts to full height at both rail ends and connect the bars to them with welded or bolted caps.
Add bolted gusset plates at every diagonal crossing and leg joint, with one through-bolt at each crossing.
Add angle brackets from each leg head to the catwalk stringers and from the cab posts to the deck.
Commit to one material: timber with end checks and bolt plates, or galvanised steel; replace the roof blotches with sheet-lap streaks.
Frame the stair opening with trimmers and a guard rail; remove the other holes.

defects: Gate, real floater: side windows (audit groups at +/-0.75, 1.55, 0.09), view 6: flat black rectangles hover outside the curved cab skin with exposed corners.
Gate, real floater: tailgate (audit group at 0.01, 0.61, -2.66), views 1, 2, 5: hangs at an angle with no hinges or chains, cutting across the bed floor edge.

Gate, real floater: door/running-board groups (+/-0.92, 0.87, 0.14) and front bumper (0, 0.64, 2.57), views 3-4 and 6: running board and bumper have no hangers or brackets. Mirrors at +/-1.0, 1.53, 0.52 sit on stubs that stop short of the door.
Audit false positive or minor: tail light and door handle groups are small mounted parts.
Paint, views 1-6: tan and blue patches at the same size and density on every panel read as military camouflage; nothing follows edges, seams or low points.
Front fenders, views 3-4 and front crop: thin arcs with daylight between arch and hood; no inner wheel well.
Rear fenders, views 1, 2, 5: duplicated inside the bed as hoops with no wheel-tub panel.
Windshield, views 3-4: replaced by a shelf-like visor plate; the cab has no glass, pillars or wipers.
Cab, view 6: bread-loaf shape with a stray triangular shard at the windshield corner.
Headlight, front crop: a glossy black blob; grille is a stuck-on slatted box.
Tyres, views 1-4: smooth with no tread; the chassis shows no springs or driveline.
fixes: Cut real window openings in the cab with door frames, rubber seals and glass; delete the flat plates.
Model a windshield with A-pillars and a split centre bar, and remove the visor plate.
Hinge the tailgate at the bed floor and hang it on two chains.
Mount the running boards and bumper on three visible brackets each.
Remodel front fenders as continuous skins meeting the hood and cowl, and add inner wheel tubs in the bed.
Replace the paint with one faded base coat, rust concentrated at seams, wheel arches and door bottoms, and dust in low areas.
Add tread blocks, leaf springs, a real headlight bowl and lens.

defects: Flat black slab, views 1, 2, 5: a textureless, unlit rectangle wider and taller than the structure stands at the tunnel end; reads as a missing asset or placeholder.
Gate, real floater: ore cart body (audit group at 0, 0.89, 3.1), crop of view 6: the box hovers above thin axle rods with no chassis or bearings.
Audit false positives: track group (y 0.09+) rests on the ties, and the ore chunks in the cart at y 1.07+ read as a load.
Portal, views 3-4: reads as a long plank shed; no timber sets, no rock face, no descent.
Walls, views 1, 2, 6: repeated board texture with sky-coloured slits between upper boards.
Roof logs, views 1-2 and 6: identical stubs at regular spacing poke from one side only and hold nothing up.
Roof, view 5: pale bands crossing the planks have no structural cause.
Cart and rails, crop of view 6: black and orange camouflage blotches on every face; pale toy-like wheels that do not sit on the rails.
Sign, views 2-4: smeared, illegible text on a board on a thin post.
fixes: Delete the black slab; end the tunnel in a modelled rock face or dark timbered drift with collapse debris.
Build proper timber sets: posts, caps and lagging, narrowing into the hill.
Remodel the cart with a steel tub, angle frame, leaf bearings, and flanged wheels on the rails.
Replace wall boards with 3-4 unique planks with knots and spiked ends; close the sky slits with backing lagging.
Repaint rails with brown rust and worn bright crowns; replace the sign text with a legible stencil.

defects: Silhouette, views 1, 2, 5: a 24 x 15 m rectangular block with near-vertical walls and a hard corner; reads as a concrete bunker.
Texture, views 1, 2, 4, 5: dark crack marks repeat at the same diagonal over every face.
Close-up, view 6: noisy, low-resolution blobs with thin dark slash artefacts and a stray bright sliver.
Portal, views 1, 2, 5: a perfectly rectangular notch with a stacked plank texture on the inside; no timber frame or collapse.
Portal area, view 3: a T-shaped black recess between lobes makes no geological sense.
Weathering, all views: uniform lichen with no water lines, overhang drips or ground scree.
fixes: Resculpt as a hillside outcrop: broken strata, slopes of 50-70 degrees, stepped ledges and a tapered foot with scree.
Replace the crack tile with non-repeating fracture lines following strata, plus a higher-resolution rock detail layer.
Cut an irregular portal and frame it with a timber set and rubble spill.
Add moss to ledges and dark water streaks beneath them; remove the slash artefacts.

defects: Orange tarp, views 2, 4, 6: bends in a smooth U like a skate ramp, with a pole poking through; cloth would not hold this shape.
Tent, views 2, 3, 5, 6: rigid triangular prism with camouflage-like blotches, no stakes, guy lines, door flap or sag.
Clothesline, views 1-4: a stiff rag hangs from the wire with no pegs; the posts have no bracing.
Fire pit, views 5-6: identical stones in a neat ring, charcoal in a star layout, and a thin rod stuck upright in the middle.
Green capsule with an orange disc, views 3 and 6: unidentifiable.
Cooler, view 6: flat red box with white scuffs and no handle or latch.
Layout, view 5: props spaced like a catalogue, with no sign of anyone having lived here.
Budget note: 3,764 triangles judged as a multi-object set, not a single small prop.
fixes: Remodel the tarp as a taut ridge line with tension folds, corner grommets, cords and pegs.
Rebuild the tent with sagging canvas, stitched seams, stakes, guy lines and a rolled door flap, and replace the blotches with stains near the ground.
Hang the rag with two pegs, add fold weight, and brace each post.
Use irregular stones of mixed size, a collapsed charcoal heap, and remove the rod or make it a pot tripod.
Replace the capsule with a rolled sleeping bag with straps; add handles, hinges and latches to the cooler; cluster the set around the fire.

defects: Audit false positives: the 12 listed groups (y 0.44-2.16, 8.6 m long) are logs resting on the row below; views 1-6 show no float. 17 further groups are not listed by the audit.
Moss, view 6: bright rectangular patches with hard straight edges look stamped on.
Bark, view 6: a visible texture seam repeats about every metre along each log.
Log ends, views 2 and 4: flat tan discs with no rings, saw marks or checks.
Stakes, views 1 and 6: short chock posts stop at about a third of pile height; they could not restrain the pile.
Shed wall, crop of view 3: planks are staggered with free ends and no post under them, and two different widths alternate for no reason.
Cable reel and drums, views 2, 5, 6: blotchy reel and plain red drums with no detail.
fixes: Paint moss with soft, irregular boundaries on top-facing surfaces only, thickest in the shadowed crevices.
Make bark seams invisible by staggering UV offsets per log and adding unique scars and knots.
Texture log ends with growth rings, saw kerfs, radial checks and paint marks.
Use taller stakes reaching 80 percent of pile height, angled and tied with a cable or chain.
Rebuild shed walls with uniform plank widths, each spanning at least two posts and nailed at each.

defects: Gate, real floater: pew backs (12 listed 1.8 m boards at x +/-1.4, y 1.1-1.34): not visible in any sheet view and neither hanging nor wall-mounted, so they cannot be cleared.
Audit false positives: belfry roof group (y 7.55+) sits on its posts in the view 1 crop; floor group (y 0.4+) reads as resting on the plinth. 2 further groups are not listed by the audit.
Paint, views 1 and 6: dark dashes repeat along every clapboard at the same density, giving a dalmatian pattern with no weather side.
Windows, views 1-4 and 6: solid dark plates with no tracery, lead lines or broken panes.
Interior, door crop of view 4: wall is white-speckled noise.
Roof tear, views 1 and 5: a long straight slot like a cut; the sheets at its edges do not sag.
Gable belt, views 1 and 4: a heavy dark band across the wall has no structural reason.
Fence and graves, views 2, 3, 5: straight fence with no visible gate; near-identical round-top headstones in a tidy grid.
Gate not verified: tests/traversal.test.mjs does not exist, so the door steps have no walk-through result.
fixes: Build pews as one piece with side ends, seat and back joined; check they meet the floor.
Replace the paint with peeling concentrated on the weather side and under the eaves, bare grey boards low down, and green algae near the base.
Add leaded tracery, wooden glazing bars and a few broken panes with dark interior behind.
Texture interior walls with plaster, lath and water damage; remove the speckle.
Make the roof tear irregular with sagging, bent sheets and exposed rafters.
Vary headstone shapes, sink and lean them, break the grid, and add a fence gate and one fallen section.

defects: Gate, real floater: entire roof (audit group at 0, 2.69, 0; 13 parts), views 1-2 and crop of view 6: no rafters or brackets, and a sky-coloured triangle shows between the roof and the post head.
Back slats, views 1, 2, 6: sky-coloured slits between the upper boards; the board has no backing.
Roof boards, view 1 underside: thin light lines between boards with no battens beneath.
Posters, views 3-4: strong readable content, but perfectly flat with no staples, curled corners or water ripple.
Posts, views 1-3: run straight into the ground with no footing, frost heave or soil line.
fixes: Add two rafters per post notched over the post head and bolted, plus a ridge beam and collar ties.
Back the board with a continuous plywood sheet or overlap the slats so no daylight passes.
Pin the posters with rusted staples, curl one corner and add rain ripples along the bottom edge.
Add a soil-stained band at the post base and a split at the post top.

defects: Audit clean: 0 floating groups.
Bracing, views 1-4: horizontal rings only; no diagonals, so a 5 m stand would rack.
Joints, views 2 and 6: horizontal poles pass into the legs with no notches, lashing or bolts, and a bright sliver runs along one brace in view 2.
Ladder, views 3-4: nothing ties the top to the deck, and no handhold is visible at the opening.
Wood, views 1-6: pole banding repeats and all boards share one grey tone.
Roof and cab, view 5: roof is out of frame in views 1-4; opening has no door or rail.
Gate not verified: tests/traversal.test.mjs does not exist, so the ladder has no walk-through result.
fixes: Add X-bracing on at least two faces with through-bolts at the leg crossings.
Notch horizontals into legs and add visible carriage bolts or wire lashing.
Lash or bolt the ladder head to the rim, and extend the rails 90 cm above the deck as handholds.
Vary board tones, add a replaced lighter plank, and put water staining beneath the roof line.

defects: Review framing: all six views cut off the top; the audit reports 2.3 m width, so a crossarm likely exists but cannot be judged.
Visible shaft, views 1-5: a plain straight cylinder with no taper, lean or checking.
Base, views 1-5: enters flat ground with no soil band, stain or burial line.
Step pegs, views 2 and 6: tiny dark dots at regular intervals, too small to read as climbing hardware.
fixes: Re-render with the camera framing the full 10 m height so the crossarm and insulators can be scored.
Add a slight taper and 1-2 degree lean, long vertical checks and a metal pole tag at eye height.
Darken the bottom 40 cm with a soil and creosote band and add a pole-mounted ground wire.
Enlarge the step pegs to about 15 cm and space them at a 40 cm stagger.

defects: Lid, views 1-5: the planks sit above the sides with a 5 cm black slot around the rim, held only at the corners.
Texture, views 1-6: heavy directional smear like motion blur; view 6 is unreadable.
Corners, views 1, 2, 4: pale vertical bands painted across plank ends; no corner posts in the geometry.
Moss, views 1-5: green film at even density on the lid.
Top, view 2: blown-out white patch.
Hardware, all views: no nails, straps or stencil.
fixes: Seat the lid on the side rim with two battens and nails; remove the slot, or open one plank to show contents.
Rebake the wood with sharp grain and knots at a resolution matching a prop seen from 50 cm.
Model separate corner battens with nail heads, and add a steel strap and a stencil.
Limit moss to low corners and the shaded side; correct the top face specular.

defects: Lid, views 2, 5, 6: texture spirals around the centre in a polar smear.
Body, views 1-5: tan and rust blotches at equal size over a pink-red base, reading as camouflage.
Rolling hoops, views 1-5: barely raised; no chime rim at the top.
Facets, views 1 and 6: the rim is visibly polygonal.
Bung, view 6: a lumpy, burnt-looking nut with no threaded seat.
fixes: Unwrap the lid planar and repaint it with radial pooling rust around the bung and rim.
Use a single faded paint colour, with rust at the chime, hoops and bottom edge and drips from the bung.
Add rolled chime rims, two raised hoops and a 24-sided profile.
Model a 2-inch threaded bung and a smaller vent bung, with a stencil and dents.

defects: Side panel, views 1-6: a raised rectangle of mottled brown plate, with a hard edge against clean green, like a patch pasted on; view 6 shows it standing proud.
Handle, views 1, 3, 4: leg pinches to a twisted bow-tie at the base.
Spout, views 1-6: a tilted, charred cylinder with no cap, hinge or seat.
Body, views 1-6: octagonal extrusion; no X stamp, seam weld or three-handle layout.
Wear, views 1-6: the panel is 100 percent rust and the frame almost none; no cause.
fixes: Remodel with a welded centre seam, stamped X recesses and three carry handles.
Add a cam-lock spout with a hinged cap and a retaining bar.
Replace the panel with continuous paint, wearing to rust along the seam, handles and bottom edge.
Fix the handle geometry so no face collapses.

defects: Scale, audit: 26 cm long and 7 cm across, about twice the size implied by a hand-held cartridge fuse.
Body, view 6: mottled plaster-grey with no glass, ceramic glaze or printed rating.
End caps, views 1-6: matt black bands with no metal sheen or contact wear.
Pins, view 6: short black stubs with no blade or knife contacts.
fixes: Scale to 12-15 cm, or keep the size and model it as a labelled mine-grade fuse.
Use a glazed ceramic or glass body showing a blown element, and print a rating and maker's mark.
Make caps bare brass or copper with tarnish and bright worn contacts, and add knife-blade terminals.

defects: Identity, views 1-6: no glass globe or wire guard; a dark turned shape reading as a rook or salt shaker.
Bail, views 1-6: a house-shaped polyline with sharp corners, one segment pinched and twisted at the peak (views 3, 4, 6).
Bail attachment, view 6: runs past the cap with no pivot and stops at the base.
Top, view 2: blown-out silver with a swirl smear.
Body, views 1-6: cloudy pale patches over black, 10-sided facets at the rims.
fixes: Build a kerosene lantern: font, burner, glass globe, wire guard, top vent and filler cap.
Bend the bail as a smooth wire arc pivoting in two side lugs, with a wooden grip.
Add 16+ radial segments, and repaint with sooty venting at the top and rust around the font seam.

defects: Identity, views 1-6: a green rounded box with one lens; no IR array, PIR window, latch, strap or mount.
Top, view 2: blown-out white patch.
Wear, views 1-6: orange rim on every top edge with no cause.
Placement, views 1-5: stands on the ground; a trail camera is strapped to a tree.
fixes: Add an IR LED grid, a PIR lens, a side latch, a strap slot and a textured camo moulding printed by the maker.
Add a webbing strap and a threaded mount.
Replace the edge rust with plastic scuffing and dirt in the recesses; fix the top specular.

defects: Plate, views 1-5: visible face is blank yellow with rust blots and no legend or symbol (the top edge is out of frame in every view).
Fixing, views 1-2: the pole runs behind the plate with no bracket, clamp or bolts.
Back face, views 1-2: same yellow paint as the front; real signs have bare grey backs.
Post, view 6: hard horizontal seam where rust stops at black; the post is camo-patterned black and orange.
Base, views 1, 5: enters the ground with no soil line.
Plate, views 3-4: 108 triangles total with a dead-flat plate and no rolled edge.
fixes: Add a legible warning legend, or a stencil with shot holes and sun fade.
Bolt the plate on with two U-clamps and a backing strut.
Make the back bare galvanised steel with a stencil code.
Retexture the post as galvanised pipe with rust at the clamps and ground line; fix the seam.
Render a view framing the entire plate.

defects: Identity, views 1-6: a smooth faceted torus with a 14-sided silhouette; reads as an inner tube.
Tread and sidewall, views 1-6: no tread, shoulder blocks, lettering, bead or wheel-well shape.
Crown, view 2: small triangular spikes along the widest ring.
Material, views 1-6: flat dark grey with no rubber texture, dust, cracking or mud.
Proportion, audit: 96 cm across and 19 cm tall lying flat; the section is too round.
fixes: Remodel with a square-shouldered section, tread blocks, sidewall lettering and a bead, with 32+ segments.
Add dry-rot cracks on the sidewall, a mud line and a torn section.
Fix the crown geometry.

defects: Gate, real floater: audit group at -2.35, 2.09, -3.96 is a stray zero-size mesh fragment; not a mounted part. Invisible at this scale, but it should be removed.
Silhouette, views 2 and 4: lobes are box-like with near-vertical faces and a hard V between them.
Texture, views 1, 3, 4: the same dark crack marks repeat at one diagonal.
Close-up, view 6: mottled lichen is reasonably convincing and moss sits in the crevice, but sharp black slits appear at the fold.
Surface, views 1-3: tiny bright sparkle pixels at creases.
fixes: Delete the zero-size mesh island.
Break up box lobes with chamfers, strata offsets and undercut ledges, and add a scree skirt.
Rotate crack layers per lobe; add crack strokes along the strata.
Fix slit triangles and weld the sparkle cracks.

defects: Shapes, view 5: cross-shaped plan built from intersecting slabs with hard seams.
Flipped facets, view 6: dark triangular shards at the left edge and centre.
Texture, views 1-4: dark crack marks repeat at one diagonal.
Ground contact, views 1-4: the lower edge stops abruptly on flat ground with no debris.
Audit: 2 connected parts on the ground; no floaters.
fixes: Merge the slabs into one form with weathered joints, and fix the flipped triangles.
Vary crack direction by lobe.
Add fallen stones and soil at the base.

defects: Silhouette, views 2-3: long flat-topped block with vertical walls.
Facets, view 6: a sharp pinched facet with dark inverted faces, and the texture stretches into streaks on the right.
Crease, view 1: thin pale line and sharp slivers at the top surface; view 2 shows white sparkle pixels.
Texture, view 5: repeated dark slashes on the top face, evenly spaced.
fixes: Add slumped, stepped faces and tilted strata; remove the flat top.
Rebuild the pinched facets and re-unwrap the stretched section.
Weld sparkle seams and break up the slash spacing.

defects: Gate, real floater: audit group at -1.1, 4.19, -3.47 is a stray zero-size mesh fragment; not a mounted part.
Silhouette, view 2: a near-square vertical wall facing the viewer, like a cut cube.
Spikes, views 1 and 3: sharp triangular shards stick out of the outline.
Facets, views 1-4 and 6: dozens of flipped triangles and folded shards across the surface.
Weathering, views 1-5: uniform; no water lines or moss concentrated by slope.
fixes: Delete the zero-size mesh island and remesh, removing self-intersecting shards.
Resculpt the square face with stepped strata and an undercut foot.
Add moss on the top ledges and dark water stains beneath them.
